text: i can still remember that tragic day as if it happened yesterday, and even now, the pain of it stays with me. we were at buguey beach with two of our staff members. it was supposed to be a simple stopover, just a chance to relax for a while. one of our staff decided to go into the water. three stayed on the shore , watching him. he was only about a meter away from the children playing near the sand, and from where i stood, the water looked shallow, no more than knee-deep. then everything changed in an instant. a large wave suddenly hit him. i heard him call out for help, and before we could react, another wave came. he tried a third time to jump up and call for help, but after that, we could no longer see him. the waves just kept coming. we immediately called for the lifeguard, but he was unable to reach him in time. rescuers from the mdrrmo arrived quickly with a life buoy and did everything they could, but they could not save him. divers from santa ana, cagayan were also called, but they were nearly two hours away. by then, what started as a rescue effort had sadly became a retrieval operation. his body was recovered the following day. those hours of waiting were some of the hardest moments. i remember staring at the water, praying, crying, and asking myself over and over how something so terrible could happen so fast. one moment we were all together, and the next, he was gone. the next hard thing is to call his family hoping what just happened was a nightmare.. for a long time, i carried so many questions and so much guilt. i kept wondering if there was something more i could have done. even today, whenever i hear about similar incidents, it brings me right back to that day and the heartbreak we experienced. it is a pain i would never wish on anyone. more than anything, i hope no family ever has to endure that kind of loss. prayers for healing on both side. :red_heart:
